stories.title: Jev is probably Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
stories.reason: Rigorous statistical fingerprinting (tokenizer correlation, throughput, latency, self-ID probes) identifies a closed model's hidden identity as Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; methodologically strong eval-transparency work.
key_facts: 9,976-request latency study: median 77->155ms across 2k-token buckets, p50-p99 gap 47-58ms, consistent with sparse MoE
Across 22 prompt variants Jev rejects being DeepSeek (95-98%) and Gemma (86-90%) but claims Qwen 74% of the time when asked which model it wants to be
Qwen's tokenizer correlates with Jev's latency better (Spearman) than TypeSafe's own reported token counts; long prompts differ by ~2000 tokens
Prefill throughput on 250 prompts tracks a self-hosted Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (Mo Lite) most closely, gap shrinking from 22% to 7% as tokens grow; dense 27B plateaus near 35K tok/s vs Jev's 90K+

stories.title: Microsoft: China’s Salt Typhoon hackers are using Artex
stories.reason: Microsoft officially attributes Chinese state actors Salt Typhoon/Crystal Typhoon's use of the AI-driven pentest tool Artex for recon, credential attacks and web exploitation, tied to the 2024 US telecom breach and prior ConnectWise supply-chain attack — a concrete, large-scale AI-offense story with primary-source attribution.
key_facts: Microsoft: Salt Typhoon/Crystal Typhoon added Artex for network recon, credential attacks, web app exploitation
Artex released in July 2026; FBI issued an advisory on it ~2 weeks before Microsoft's report
NYT/NextGov reported alleged use against CIA, NGA, and ODNI; also linked to attacks on South Korean/Japanese financial institutions
Salt Typhoon tied to 2024 breach of 9+ US telecoms; original Chinese researcher pulled the source from GitHub but copies/commercial resales circulate

stories.title: 180B Parameters, 32GB of RAM: Pushing MoE Inference to the Limit with Transformers
stories.reason: Expert-streaming technique runs a 180B-parameter MoE model on 32GB of RAM via selective expert offloading/quantization with concrete throughput numbers against a known baseline — squarely in Mine's top-priority inference-serving/quantization category.
key_facts: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (180B) runs on a 32GB Mac M5 via expert streaming (hot experts cached, rest read from SSD on demand)
Experts quantized to 3-bit (49GB disk / 12GiB cached); dense layers 8-bit with ~0.2% perplexity increase vs BF16
Final throughput: 13.9 tok/s decode (200 tok), 228 tok/s prefill (4K prompt) — within ~6% of the Strata baseline

stories.title: Novita, StreamLake, etc. are ByteDance Ark wrappers
stories.reason: Strong investigative piece fingerprinting Novita/StreamLake/Ant Digital as ByteDance Ark (Doubao) wrappers via network origin, ID formats, censorship behavior and pricing — exactly the 'how models are actually served' transparency story Mine values, with a reproducible public probe.
key_facts: StreamLake/Novita downloads trace to Volcano Engine (Beijing) and BytePlus (Singapore) ByteDance infrastructure
Upstream IDs follow ByteDance's Ark format ('call_00_' prefixes); error messages match word-for-word across providers
Models refuse Tank Man/June 4 1989 questions with ByteDance's canned Chinese refusal text
Author published a reproducible GitHub probe testing every OpenRouter host of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash

stories.title: 1Password Security Incident
stories.reason: Major 1Password breach (employee GitHub account -> source code, CI/CD secrets, subset of customer account metadata) — large enough to run as a headline despite no AI angle and heavy HN saturation (1463 pts).
key_facts: Attacker used a compromised employee GitHub account to push malicious code into backend CI/CD with access to admin data
Exposed: names/emails, account IDs, public keys/SRP params, some invitation/recovery tokens, private source code; vault contents/keys not affected
1Password lengthened recovery codes to 10 alphanumeric chars; full root-cause analysis still pending

stories.title: Italy and Switzerland warn of autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks
stories.reason: Italian and Swiss CERTs report concrete, observed autonomous-AI-agent attack campaigns (multi-agent coordinators, real-time code generation to evade defenses) against live infrastructure, naming four specific AI pentest/red-team tools — substantive, not a vague policy statement.
key_facts: Italy: a DeepSeek Harness setup used a coordinator assigning 5 agents (recon/exploitation/persistence) that compromised many systems within a few hours
Switzerland: first reports of AI-agent-assisted attacks on critical infrastructure across 2+ sectors; every known case succeeded
Named tools: ARTEX AI, CyberStrikeAI, DeepSeek Harness (Red Team), PentAGI
Switzerland says the number of publicly available AI agents has nearly doubled since October

stories.title: Bare Metal Qwen
stories.reason: Novel bare-metal engineering feat: Qwen3-0.6B running directly on x86-64 hardware with no OS/libc, with concrete boot and decode-speed numbers.
key_facts: 24KB assembly kernel boots to interactive LLM prompt in 74-94ms
QEMU/KVM AMD EPYC 7642, 16 vCPUs: ~135 tok/s decode; Proxmox Xeon E5-2670 v3, 12 cores: ~55 tok/s decode
Model: Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, 614-649MB, mapped zero-copy via 2MiB hugepages, ~449MB KV-cache arena, 2048-token context
Author claims it beats Linux-based version and llama.cpp CPU Q8_0 at every thread count (unverified)

stories.title: AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp
stories.reason: AMD-specific llama.cpp patch set roughly doubles prefill and generation throughput on RDNA hardware with concrete before/after numbers — solid, on-topic inference-serving engineering, though from a single user's benchmark.
key_facts: On an AMD R9700 eGPU running Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B Q6_K_L with MTP: prefill ~700->~1300 tok/s, generation ~35->~55 tok/s
